posts.style: Design & Aspiration · The Kitchen That Faces the Fire
posts.alt: A modern La Jolla hillside backyard at golden hour under a black aluminum StruXure louvered pergola with recessed downlights, over a large-format warm-grey porcelain terrace: a sand-toned outdoor kitchen with a stainless Lynx built-in grill and cabinetry along one side, a bar counter with black barstools, a board-formed concrete linear fire table burning beside a cushioned concrete bench, olive trees and agave in large planters, a two-story white stucco contemporary home with black-framed windows, and neighboring hillside homes on both sides stepping down toward the Pacific
posts.hook: Most outdoor kitchens are built with their back to the party. This one isn't.
posts.caption:
Look at where the grill sits. It opens straight onto the fire table and the bench, a step from the conversation instead of pushed against a far wall. That single decision is what turns a kitchen into the middle of the evening instead of a job someone does on the edge of it.

Everything else follows from it. The louvered roof opens for winter sun and closes for a July afternoon, with lighting built into the blades so the room doesn't go dark at six. The linear fire table runs parallel to the bench, so the seating reads as one long conversation rather than a circle of chairs. The porcelain underfoot doesn't stain when the wine does, and the concrete, stone and stucco stay in the same quiet palette as the house.

Nothing here is loud. It's just arranged around how people actually stand, cook and linger.

The selections:
• StruXure louvered pergola with integrated downlights
• large-format porcelain pavers
• Lynx built-in grill & stainless cabinetry
• board-formed concrete linear fire table & bench
• potted olive trees & agave

posts.alt: A San Miguel Ranch backyard at dusk with a round Belgard paver fire circle set into a wide SYNLawn artificial lawn, a stone-clad gas fire pit burning at the center, four cushioned wicker lounge chairs with folded throws, cedar raised planters with young citrus trees along a wood fence, ornamental grasses, cafe string lights on wood posts, a sand-stucco tile-roof home, and neighboring two-story tile-roof houses close by on both sides and beyond the back fence
posts.hook: The best seat in the house in November is outside, about four feet from a fire.
posts.caption:
Evenings in San Diego get short this time of year, but they don't get cold enough to send you in. What they need is a reason to stay out.

This yard gives it one. A paver circle set right into the lawn, a gas fire that lights with a switch, and four deep chairs pulled close enough to talk without raising your voice. The lawn stays green without a sprinkler schedule, so the kids have somewhere to run while the adults don't move. Cedar planters along the fence hold citrus and grasses at eye level, and the string lights give the whole thing a ceiling once the sky goes blue.

A normal suburban lot. A very good reason to skip the couch.

The selections:
• Belgard paver fire circle
• stone-clad gas fire pit
• SYNLawn artificial turf
• cedar raised planters with citrus & ornamental grasses
• cafe string lighting

posts.style: Seasonal · Veterans Day · Point Loma Curb Appeal
posts.alt: The front of a Point Loma coastal cottage at golden hour: white lap siding, a grey shingle roof, a navy blue front door with brass hardware and an American flag on the white-columned porch, a warm-grey Techo-Bloc slab driveway and walk with green dymondia joints, a board-formed concrete planter wall with an olive tree, agave, lavender and grasses, bougainvillea over the side fence, low path lights, a tall Torrey pine and a glimpse of San Diego Bay, with neighboring homes close by on both sides
posts.hook: Today, a quiet thank you from a city built around those who served.
posts.caption:
San Diego is a Navy town, and Point Loma wears that history closer than most. Its streets run down toward the bay, past the base and the white rows of Fort Rosecrans, and plenty of the families on them have given years of service to the rest of us.

So today isn't a day for selling anything. It's a day to say thank you — to the veterans in our neighborhoods, in our clients' homes, and in our own families. We're grateful to do our work in a city you helped shape.

The front of the house is where every homecoming starts. Here it's kept simple: a flag on the porch, wide slab pavers with a green ribbon of groundcover in every joint, a low concrete planter wall holding an olive tree and drought planting, and low lights that walk you to the door after dark.

The selections:
• Techo-Bloc Blu 60 slab driveway with dymondia joints
• board-formed concrete planter wall
• olive, bougainvillea & lavender
• FX Luminaire path lights

If you're thinking about the front of your own home, DM “DESIGN” whenever you're ready.

posts.style: Craft & Process · Where the Water Goes
posts.alt: A narrow North Park side courtyard at twilight beside a sage-green craftsman bungalow with white trim: large-format light grey porcelain pavers with a slim linear channel drain along the foundation, a stained cedar pergola strung with cafe lights, a dark stone water bowl on river rock, a living green wall along a cedar fence, Meyer lemon trees in terracotta pots, a detached garage at the back, and neighboring bungalow and Spanish tile rooflines, mature trees and power lines beyond the fence
posts.hook: On a small lot, water has nowhere to go but where you send it.
posts.caption:
A big yard forgives a lot. A 30-foot courtyard between a bungalow and a garage forgives nothing — get the fall wrong by a fraction and the first real rain ends up against the house.

So the part of this job you'll never notice is the part that matters most. The porcelain is set on a compacted base with a slight, deliberate pitch away from the foundation, and every surface is planned to hand its water to a drain — here, the slim channel drain running along the house — or a planting bed before it reaches a wall. Large-format porcelain helps: fewer joints, a surface that won't absorb or stain, and a finish that stays grippy when wet. Only once the water has a path do the finishes arrive — the cedar pergola, the stone water bowl, the green wall, the citrus in terracotta.

The pretty part took a weekend to style. The grading is why it'll still look like this in ten years.

The selections:
• large-format porcelain pavers
• stained cedar pergola with cafe lighting
• Bobe-style stone water bowl on river rock
• living green wall
• potted Meyer lemon & citrus in terracotta

posts.style: Trust & Difference · Drone Aerial · Your Address Stays Yours
posts.alt: Top-down drone aerial of a Carmel Valley backyard with a blue and grey VersaCourt half-court for basketball and pickleball in a light paver border, a basketball hoop at one end, a wide SYNLawn artificial lawn around the court, agave, blue fescue and succulent borders along the block walls, the home's grey concrete-tile roof along the bottom edge, and neighboring backyards with pools and patios and tile rooftops on every side
posts.hook: You won't find our clients' addresses on this page. That's on purpose.
posts.caption:
A lot of contractors will happily send you to drive past their last job. We won't — and we'd rather tell you why than be vague about it.

The homes we work on belong to families, not to our marketing. Nobody should find a stranger slowing down outside their house because a contractor used it as a showroom. So when you're considering working with us, you get written references and a detailed photographic record during discovery, and the people who live there get left alone. It's the same discretion we'll show your home once it's finished.

This is the kind of view you'll see from us: the whole design, top-down, and not a house number in sight. A half-court set in a clean paver frame, turf to soften every edge, and drought planting that holds the boundary without a single hedge to trim.

The selections:
• VersaCourt basketball & pickleball court tiles
• paver border & court surround
• SYNLawn artificial turf
• agave, blue fescue & succulent borders

References available on request. Want to talk through your own yard? DM “DESIGN”.
